liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Walkin' Blues** (1 review, 1 other source): Boz Scaggs sings lead; solos go to Brent on Hammond B3, then Jerry, then John Cippolina; The previous Walkin' Blues was on 10/07/66 [1][15]
- **Althea** (1 review): Althea was the only slow song in an otherwise fast set, and it still rocked [16]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Jerry plays two strong solos in Not Fade Away [15]
- **A Mind To Give Up Livin'** (1 review): This song gave the reviewer a feeling of impending doom, like an earthquake [12]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): During Lovelight the reviewer felt they were watching Pigpen play keyboard [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Boz Scaggs introduced by Bob Weir**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **A Mind To Give Up Livin'**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Walkin' Blues [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-05-28.senn441.unknown.87547.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 15 songs; 93 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1982-05-28.sbd.tobin.130199.flac16**: soundboard; 14 songs; 96 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1982-05-28.sbd.latvala-lee-smith.131808.flac16**: soundboard; 14 songs; 98 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd82-05-28.nak300.dgrabski.10974.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 9 songs; 62 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [11]. Said about its sound: The Nakamichi audience tape sounds excellent, with clear lead guitar lines [15]

## Around the show

- The Dead were not the headliners that night; the reviewer says the Airplane existed again [12]
- The show was a Vietnam Vets benefit, and Country Joe played the Fixin' To Die Rag [13]
- The Dead were not the headliners but were the highlight; the reviewer travelled from Boulder after the Greek shows [13]
- The Dead lost a coin flip with the Starship and played second billing; Country Joe opened [16]
- Someone ad-libs a line about Sweet Jane having a sex change [17]
- The crowd energy was wild, but the hall's sound was poor for the first four or five songs [19]
- A Vietnam Vets benefit where Country Joe played the Fixin' To Die Rag; the Dead were not the headliners [21]
- The headliner was the Starship, without Jorma or Jack [21]
- The reviewer calls the Boz Scaggs and Cipollina set the strongest blues set they have ever seen [16]
- Disputes that this was the first Lovelight since Pigpen; says one came the prior year at an Amsterdam show [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-05-28.senn441.unknown.87547.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Alex Ford; source: Unknown Audience Tape [1]. Also: Source cassette provided by Mark McCue; transfer, edits and conversion by Alex Ford in September 2007; tape flip during Drums [1]
- **gd1982-05-28.sbd.tobin.130199.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: flac16; (original shnid = 11362) SBD:Unknown Gen Cassette>CD; Benefit for Vietnam Veterans with guests; See info file for details; Seeded to etree by Jim… [2]. Also: A mix by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in June 2014 by Trader Little Helper [2]
- **gd1982-05-28.sbd.latvala-lee-smith.131808.flac16**: taped by Dick Latvala -> Pat Lee; transferred by Matt Smith; source: SBD: It's from a Pat Lee reel, Dick Latvala gave it to him. Maybe MC>R @3 3/4ips?? Maybe one more gen; Transfer info: Akai GX636 direct tape head output >… [3]
- **gd82-05-28.nak300.dgrabski.10974.sbefail.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Nak 300's [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Mo: [Grateful Dead Vintage Concert Poster from Moscone Center, May 28, 1982 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/posters-handbills-and-postcards/grateful-dead/poster/MOS820528-01.html) [25]
